title: 55-year-old woman with a problem in her left hand
arrival: A 55-year-old woman presents with a problem in her left hand that began this morning.
keyCriterion: Yellow — Disability: acute focal neurologic complaint
feedbackWhy: She has numbness and tingling in her left hand that began this morning. This is an acute focal neurological complaint, which meets a yellow Disability criterion. No red criterion is met. She should be moved to the clinical treatment area.
reviewNote: CLINICIAN REVIEW REQUIRED: confirm that numbness and tingling in one hand is a good example of an acute focal neurologic complaint, or replace it with a finding you prefer. Every value is proposed.

design.intendedChallenge: An acute focal neurological complaint is a yellow Disability criterion, even in a patient who is alert and has normal vital signs.
design.expectedCommonError: triaging as green because she is alert and well appearing.

airway_red.text: Speaks in full sentences. No stridor. No respiratory distress. No central cyanosis.

circulation_red.text: Pulse strong. Capillary refill 2 seconds. No bleeding.

disability_red.text: No convulsions. Alert with normal mental status. No headache. No stiff neck.

other_red.text: Age 55. No chest or abdominal pain. No trauma, poisoning, threatened limb or snake bite. Not aggressive.

airway_yellow.text: No swelling of the mouth, throat or neck. No wheezing.

circulation_yellow.text: No vomiting or diarrhoea. No bleeding or fainting. Not pale. Drinking normally.

disability_yellow.text: Numbness and tingling in the left hand since this morning. Grip strength normal. Speech clear. No weakness in the other limbs. No visual disturbance. No pain.

other_yellow.text: No rash, deformity, fracture or dislocation. No trauma. No known surgical diagnosis. Passing urine normally. No bite or needlestick exposure.
